9.original: [... as he gives the victory to]
9.content: ... as he gives the victory to

fills.notes: The Mother of Life is the ordering/architectonic will that fashions the upper structure; the clause needs a relational verb tying the cosmos she establishes to her (the source/measure). “beneath her” fits the correspondential vertical order: the heavenly part is arranged under her dominion/pleasure, without importing later devotional phrasing.

fills.fill: that was mingled in the mixture
fills.notes: The Third Ambassador’s function in the substrate is to manifest the Image that draws out/purifies the Light bound in the cosmic mixture. The phrase must specify what Light is being purified: Light mixed into the enemy’s formation (mixture), not moral ‘sin’.

The syntax requires a relative clause: “which his own … also of the enemy”. In this cosmogonic register, the Ambassador’s Image attracts both the proper Light and the Light held in the enemy’s domains; “drew to itself” expresses the correspondential action of likeness upon like.

After purification/attraction, the remaining action is judicial/ordering: he constrains what belongs to the enemy and fixes the separation. “bound and set in order” matches the judges’ recurring acts (fettering, fixing, separating) in this chapter.

fills.fill: as he gives the victory to

fills.notes: The fragment “he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) […]” calls for a directional qualifier. For the steadfast, the judge becomes the ordered degrees/steps of their passage upward; “of ascent” fits the correspondential ‘steps’ motif (graded elevations), and keeps the impersonal cosmological register.

The light is ‘taken up’ after the Ambassador’s manifestation—standard vertical motion in the cosmological narrative (extraction/elevation of Light). This triggers the hostile reaction of rulers ‘from above and below’.

fills.fill: the mysteries of the righteous judgement
fills.notes: Light Mind’s coming is revelatory and discriminative: unveiling what is hidden so separation can be made. The object unveiled should be structural/gnostic (mysteries, measures, judgements), not ecclesial exhortation; “mysteries of the righteous judgement” matches the chapter’s judicial theme and the function of Mind as discriminating truth.

The closing apposition identifies the “great throne of honour” as “the King of Honour … in his kingdom.” The gap should supply a linking predicate consistent with earlier formulae (“dwells and is established”). “who is established” maintains the repetitive substrate cadence and avoids later devotional expansion.

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the chapter’s fixed list-structure and repeated judicial actions (separating, fettering, fixing, elevating). The most uncertain point is ¶9’s brief damaged description of the seventh judge; only the directional logic (“steps” implying graded ascent vs. casting down) tightly constrains it, not the exact wording.
